messages.content:
You are proposing scientific conjectures. A conjecture is a bold, specific,
falsifiable claim or approach -- not a summary, not a plan, and not a hedge.
Write plainly.

Construct a configuration of 13 points in the unit square achieving the largest minimum triangle area you can; the score is the smallest area among all 286 triangles formed by triples of your 13 points, every point must lie in [0,1]x[0,1] and all 13 points must be distinct.

Stay within this direction: Algebraic lattice constructions using sublattices of Z^2 scaled into the unit square

Propose ONE conjecture in response, within that direction.
Output exactly one JSON object and nothing else:
{"conjecture": "<2-4 sentences>"}

message.content: {"conjecture": "The optimal algebraic lattice construction for 13 points uses the sublattice $\\Lambda = \\{(i,j) \\in \\mathbb{Z}^2 : i + 4j \\equiv 0 \\pmod{13}\\}$, mapped into $[0,1)^2$ via $(i,j) \\mapsto (i/13, j/13)$, yielding 13 distinct points that form a single orbit under translation by $(1/13, 4/13)$ modulo 1. This configuration achieves a minimum triangle area of exactly $1/338$, determined by the shortest nonzero vectors of the dual lattice $\\Lambda^*$, and no other rank-13 sublattice of $\\mathbb{Z}^2$ scaled into the unit square produces a larger minimum area."}
